settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: The entity may already have been parsed by the framework before reaching this provider, so the parser may only see already-resolved data.
SourceProvider.readFrom itself does not parse (returns a StreamSource of the raw stream); other code paths may parse with hardened factories.
Many modern JDK/JAXP defaults and container settings may already disable external entity resolution.
DOM/SAX parsing here occurs during serialization (write), not necessarily directly reachable from raw remote input.
candidates.description: SourceProvider is a JAX-RS @Provider handling XML media types. In writeTo, when the source is a StreamSource it constructs a new SAX parser via SAXParserFactory.newInstance() and wraps the stream in a SAXSource, then transforms it. Within the read span, no JAXP features/attributes (secure processing, disallow-doctype-decl, external-general/parameter-entities) are set on this SAXParserFactory, so hardening is not evident in this file. Whether external entities are resolved then depends on the JAXP default XMLReader of the deployment, which for some implementations resolves external DTDs/general entities, potentially yielding an SSRF/local-file-disclosure path when this Source is parsed. Note setSystemId is also taken from the source during this construction.
missing_evidence: No traced call site showing attacker-controlled InputStream reaching SourceProvider.writeTo with a StreamSource of raw request bytes.
No confirmation of default SAXParserFactory external-entity behavior in the deployment target.
No repository test/config asserting this provider's parser is hardened.
preconditions: An application exposes a JAX-RS resource handling javax.xml.transform.Source such that writeTo is invoked with a StreamSource.
A StreamSource built from the request entity stream reaches writeTo (e.g., a resource that consumes Source and writes it back).
The default SAXParserFactory in the runtime resolves external entities (implementation-dependent).
candidates.title: SourceProvider.writeTo creates SAX parser without explicit XXE hardening

counter_evidence: Defaults in the read span are the safe values (expandEntityReferences=false, enableSecureProcessingFeature=true, disableDTDs=true).
Setting expandEntityReferences=true is a documented backward-compatibility mechanism requiring an explicit, trusted configuration change.
FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING remains enabled by default, which in many parsers limits external access even if DTDs are allowed.
candidates.description: DocumentProvider parses request XML into a DOM Document. Within the read span, its DocumentBuilderFactory is created in lazyInit() and its security features are set inside readFrom (setExpandEntityReferences, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities, external-parameter-entities). The expandEntityReferences, enableSecureProcessingFeature and disableDTDs fields default to safe values but are each overridable from ResteasyConfiguration parameters (RESTEASY_EXPAND_ENTITY_REFERENCES, RESTEASY_SECURE_PROCESSING_FEATURE, RESTEASY_DISABLE_DTDS). When expandEntityReferences is enabled, the code sets accessExternalDTD to "all" and enables external general/parameter entities, which reintroduces external entity resolution (file/SSRF). This is a configuration-dependent weakening rather than an unconditional flaw, but the 'all' accessExternalDTD plus enabled external entities is worth flagging.
missing_evidence: No evidence that an untrusted remote actor can set the RESTEASY_EXPAND_ENTITY_REFERENCES configuration parameter.
No traced request mapping demonstrating an endpoint accepting Document.
Behavior under non-default configurations was not tested/verified in the reviewed code.
preconditions: A JAX-RS resource consumes application/xml (or *+xml) into an org.w3c.dom.Document so DocumentProvider.readFrom is selected.
An administrator (or actor able to control RESTEasy context configuration) sets resteasy.expand.entity.references=true (or secure.processing.feature=false / disable.dtds=false).
The runtime JAXP implementation honors the external-entity/accessExternalDTD settings.
candidates.title: DocumentProvider XXE protections are configuration-overridable

counter_evidence: The provider is @Deprecated and, per the Javadoc in the read span, disabled by default requiring explicit registration.
No annotation-based auto-registration forcing its use was found in the read spans.
candidates.description: SerializableProvider implements a MessageBodyReader for media type application/x-java-serialized-object and calls ObjectInputStream.readObject() on the request entity stream in readFrom. Deserializing untrusted Java streams is dangerous (gadget chains). Within the read span, the class is @Deprecated and its Javadoc states it is disabled by default and requires explicit registration. This is a documented, opt-in unsafe provider; flagged as residual risk only if an application enables it.
missing_evidence: No repository evidence that the provider is registered by default in a shipped configuration.
No traced endpoint consuming Serializable that would select this reader in a default deployment.
preconditions: Application explicitly registers SerializableProvider (via META-INF/services or explicit registration).
A resource consumes a Serializable-typed body with media type application/x-java-serialized-object.
A malicious serialized payload with a usable gadget chain on the classpath is sent.
candidates.title: SerializableProvider performs Java deserialization (deprecated, documented as disabled by default)
